title: Extra Example C
summary: The height bisects the base, making a right-angled triangle.
alt: Extra Example C: A tent is an isosceles triangle with equal sides 6.5 m and base 5 m. Calculate the height of the tent.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A tent is an **isosceles triangle TUV** with equal sloping sides **TU = TV = 6.5 m** and base **UV = 5 m**. The height **TH** drops to the midpoint **H** of the base, so **∠H = 90°**. Find the height of the tent.

steps.title: The height bisects the base
steps.narration: In an isosceles triangle the height to the base cuts it in **half**.\[\begin{aligned}\role{legA}{UH} &= \tfrac{1}{2}\times 5 = \role{legA}{2.5}\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔTUH, **∠H = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **TU**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Make the unknown the subject
steps.narration: We want a **shorter side**, so subtract the known square from the hypotenuse square.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TU^2} - \role{legA}{UH^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TU^2} - \role{legA}{UH^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{6.5^2} - \role{legA}{2.5^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{TU^2} &= \role{legA}{UH^2} + \role{legB}{TH^2} \\ \role{legB}{TH^2} &= \role{hyp}{TU^2} - \role{legA}{UH^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{6.5^2} - \role{legA}{2.5^2} \\ &= \role{hyp}{42.25} - \role{legA}{6.25} \\ &= \role{legB}{36} \\ \role{legB}{TH} &= \sqrt{36} = \role{ans}{6\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse **10 m** and one shorter side **6 m**. Find the other shorter side.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find a shorter side: **subtract** the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the **square root**.
A shorter side must be **smaller** than the hypotenuse — a quick check on your answer.

notes.title: Isosceles trick
notes.text: The height from the apex of an isosceles triangle **bisects** the base, so the half-base and the height are the two shorter sides.
